content:
This is a Sumerian mythological text that appears to describe primordial times and the actions of various deities. Here's my translation:

1. From the day of old, from that day when heaven and earth were [created],
2. From the night of old, from that night when heaven and earth were [created],
3. [From the year] of old, when destiny was [decreed],
4. When the [An]unna gods were born,
5. When Ama-Inana took on divine authority,
6. When Ama-Inana distributed heaven and earth,
7. When Ama-Inana [...] gave birth to [something],
8. When the gods bound their banquet offerings to their shrines(?),
9. When the numerous gods were dwelling in their places, the small gods were carrying clay,
10. When the gods were digging the rivers, piling up their earth,
11. When the gods were doing the digging, establishing their life force through work,
12. At that time, Enlil, the wise one who possesses vast intelligence, was present among the numerous gods,
13. Enki made the Abzu, the abyss of sweet waters, a place where no god would disturb his heart,
14. He lay down to sleep, and no one dared to rise,
15. The gods were weeping and lamenting, they were doing hard labor,
16. When humans were lying down to sleep, they could not rise from their sleeping place,
17. Namma, the mother who gave birth to the leaders and the numerous gods,
18. Brought the tears of the gods to her son,
19. "You lie sleeping, but why don't you rise from sleep?
20. [Something] ... will not rise,
21. The form you have created, ... its neck/back they are making good."

Note: This text contains several damaged or unclear passages marked with brackets and question marks. The translation represents the general meaning based on context and parallel texts, but some details remain uncertain due to the condition of the source material.
